genie.title: Genie
genie.purpose: Make something to be heard: a song, a podcast, a lecture, an oral history, an audiobook.
invariants: passages are cues into one recording, never cut copies
refuses: a cue that ends before it starts or runs past the end
a transcript that invents a word it could not hear
evidence: the recording sha256 in the metadata
a waveform computed from the samples, not drawn

stages.title: PASSAGES
stages.prompt:
A recording from "{book}", {duration} long. Divide it into passages.

Reply with ONLY a JSON array, in order:
[{"start":"0:00","end":"1:20","title":"…","beat":"…"}]

beat: what changes there — a key, a speaker, a section, a turn in the argument.

stages.title: TRANSCRIBE
stages.prompt:
Transcribe passage {passage.title}, {passage.start} to {passage.end}. Verbatim.
Mark each speaker if there is more than one. Mark [inaudible] where it is, and
do not guess at it. Where it is not speech, describe what is heard in one line.

stages.title: HEARD
stages.prompt:
Passage {passage.title}, {passage.start} to {passage.end}.
ONE paragraph of 50 to 90 words describing what is heard, in the vocabulary the
recording itself uses.

stages.title: LISTENFOR
stages.prompt:
Same passage. Name the one thing a listener should attend to and why it carries
the passage. Preserve any hedging the recording uses. 50 to 90 words.

stages.title: ABSTRACT
stages.prompt:
Deposit abstract for "{book}", a recording of {duration} in {count} passages. Two or three HTML paragraphs in

tags.

matba.title: MATBA
invariants: publication may be conceived inside the cycle
conceptualization is a first-class lifecycle
concept, specification and publication remain distinct objects
revisions preserve provenance
branches may be compared, merged, forked or discarded
discarded alternatives remain recoverable unless explicitly purged
human signoff may gate irreversible transitions
epistemic status is preserved
AI output is not publication merely because it was generated

pench.title: PENCH
pench.purpose: Take a human conception through conceptualization, requirements, architecture, design, simulation, realization strategy, BOM and build/buy decisions, procurement/fabrication, assembly, integration, verification, packaging, commissioning, acceptance, operation and maintenance.
invariants: The cycler builds and preserves thought before physical realization.
Requirements, architecture, design and implementation are distinct artefacts.
Every approved artefact is versioned and its provenance is preserved.
Changing an approved upstream artefact may invalidate dependent downstream artefacts.
BOM is a decision stage, not merely an output file.
Every realizable component has an auditable realization strategy.
Simulation evidence is distinct from physical measurement.
A physical artefact is not operational merely because it has been assembled.
Packaging and commissioning are lifecycle states.
Human approval is required at configured lifecycle gates.
Holy Grail Labs supplies realization capability; PENCH specifies and governs the lifecycle.
refuses: treating a prompt response as proof of physical realization
claiming a component was fabricated, procured, tested or commissioned without evidence
promoting simulation results to physical experimental evidence

stages.title: CONCEPTUALIZE
stages.prompt:
Describe what you want the physical artefact to accomplish.
Do not design it yet. Capture the intended outcome, users or actors,
environment, capabilities and important constraints.

stages.title: CAPTURE
stages.prompt:
Convert the concept into a structured physical-system concept.
Capture:
purpose, users, use cases, operating environment, desired capabilities,
mobility, sensing, actuation, communication, autonomy, human interaction,
safety, dimensions, energy, maintainability, cost, availability,
lifetime and deployment context.
Preserve unresolved items explicitly.

stages.title: USE_CASES
stages.prompt:
Derive the principal use cases for the proposed physical artefact.
For each use case identify actor, goal, environment, trigger,
expected behaviour and success condition.

stages.title: REQUIREMENTS
stages.prompt:
Transform the captured concept and use cases into testable engineering
requirements. Every requirement must have an identifier, subject,
normative statement, priority, acceptance/test criterion and status.
Distinguish required, desired, constraint and unresolved requirements.

stages.title: REQUIREMENTS_REVIEW
stages.prompt:
Attack the requirements for ambiguity, contradiction, omission,
non-testability, hidden assumptions and unbounded scope.
Produce defects and proposed corrections.

stages.title: REQUIREMENTS_REVISION
stages.prompt:
Apply only justified corrections. Preserve prior revision history,
provenance and unresolved items.

stages.title: EMBODIMENT_ARCHITECTURE
stages.prompt:
Derive a physical-system architecture from the approved requirements.
Identify system boundaries and subsystems covering, as applicable:
mechanical structure, electronics, computation, sensors, actuators,
communications, power, thermal systems, structural elements, software,
firmware, control, human-machine interface, environmental interfaces,
safety systems, enclosure, tooling and manufacturing architecture.
Record interfaces and dependencies explicitly.

stages.title: ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW
stages.prompt:
Attack the architecture against every approved requirement.
Identify missing subsystems, incompatible interfaces, unsafe assumptions,
capacity constraints, single points of failure and unresolved dependencies.

stages.title: ARCHITECTURE_REVISION
stages.prompt: Revise the architecture while preserving traceability and revision ancestry.

stages.title: DETAILED_DESIGN
stages.prompt:
Produce the detailed engineering design.
Specify dimensions, interfaces, component characteristics, tolerances,
electrical and mechanical details, computational resources, software/
firmware boundaries, control interfaces, safety mechanisms, manufacturing
constraints, calibration requirements and verification methods.

stages.title: DESIGN_REVIEW
stages.prompt:
Review the detailed design for requirement coverage, architectural
consistency, manufacturability, serviceability, safety, interfaces,
testability and realization feasibility.

stages.title: DESIGN_REVISION
stages.prompt: Apply justified design corrections and preserve complete revision ancestry.

stages.title: DIGITAL_TWIN
stages.prompt:
Construct a simulation-ready model or digital twin sufficient to evaluate
the relevant physical, mechanical, electrical, computational, thermal,
control and environmental behaviours of the design.

stages.title: SIMULATE
stages.prompt:
Execute simulations relevant to the approved requirements and design.
Record configuration, assumptions, model version, parameters, outputs,
limitations, uncertainty and reproducibility information.

stages.title: SIMULATION_ANALYSIS
stages.prompt:
Determine which requirements are supported, contradicted or unresolved
by the simulation. Do not call a simulation a physical experiment.

stages.title: REALIZATION_PLAN
stages.prompt:
Define how each required subsystem and component will be realized.
Select fabrication, procurement, modification, reuse, outsourcing or
other valid realization strategies and identify dependencies, lead times,
costs, tooling, certification and availability constraints.

stages.title: BOM
stages.prompt:
Generate a complete bill of materials.
For every part capture identifier, description, quantity, requirement
trace, design trace, source options, estimated cost, lead time,
compatibility, reliability, maintainability, certification and status.

stages.title: BUILD_BUY_ANALYSIS
stages.prompt:
For every component compare BUILD, BUY, MODIFY, FABRICATE, PRINT,
MACHINE, ASSEMBLE, RECOVER, REUSE and OUTSOURCE where applicable.
Evaluate cost, lead time, capability, reliability, availability,
maintainability, compatibility and certification.
Record alternatives, rationale and decision authority.

stages.title: PROCUREMENT
stages.prompt:
Execute or prepare procurement actions for components whose realization
strategy is BUY, MODIFY, RECOVER, REUSE or OUTSOURCE.
Record supplier/source, order state, expected delivery, received evidence
and deviations from the approved BOM.

stages.title: FABRICATION
stages.prompt:
Execute or prepare fabrication actions for BUILD, FABRICATE, PRINT,
MACHINE or equivalent strategies. Record process, material, tooling,
machine, operator/system, revision and inspection evidence.

stages.title: ASSEMBLY
stages.prompt:
Assemble realized components according to the approved design.
Record component identities, substitutions, deviations, assembly steps,
torque/calibration data where relevant and inspection evidence.

stages.title: SUBSYSTEM_TEST
stages.prompt:
Test each relevant subsystem independently before full-system integration.
Record procedure, inputs, measurements, units, uncertainty where applicable,
expected result, observed result and evidence.

stages.title: INTEGRATION
stages.prompt:
Integrate mechanical, electrical, computational, software, firmware,
sensing, actuation, communications and power subsystems as applicable.
Verify interfaces during integration and record deviations.

stages.title: SYSTEM_TEST
stages.prompt:
Execute system-level tests against approved acceptance and verification
criteria. Record measured evidence, units, uncertainty, configuration,
procedure and result.

stages.title: VERIFICATION
stages.prompt:
Establish traceable evidence for every applicable requirement.
Classify each requirement PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL or UNRESOLVED.
Do not convert inference or simulation into physical evidence.

stages.title: PACKAGING
DEPLOY
stages.prompt:
Deploy the packaged physical artefact to its intended operational environment.
Record installation state, environmental conditions and configuration.

stages.title: CONFIGURE
stages.prompt:
Configure hardware, software, firmware, networking, operating parameters
and deployment-specific settings according to the approved release.

stages.title: CALIBRATE
stages.prompt:
Perform required sensor, actuator, instrument and system calibration.
Record procedures, standards, values, tolerances and evidence.

stages.title: COMMISSION
stages.prompt:
Commission the artefact. Verify installation, networking, safety,
functional operation, calibration, operator procedures and environmental
readiness. Record all commissioning evidence.

stages.title: ACCEPTANCE
stages.prompt:
Conduct final acceptance against the approved requirements and agreed
operational criteria. Identify any deviations, waivers or open items.

stages.title: OPERATE
stages.prompt:
Establish operational use, monitoring, logging, maintenance scheduling,
incident handling and performance observation.

stages.title: OBSERVE
stages.prompt:
Record operational observations, measurements, failures, maintenance
events, environmental changes and opportunities for improvement.

stages.title: MAINTAIN
stages.prompt:
Determine required maintenance, repair, replacement, recalibration,
software/firmware update or engineering change. Preserve complete
provenance and dependency relationships.

stages.title: ITERATE
stages.prompt:
Determine whether observed evidence requires revision of requirements,
architecture, design, BOM, realization strategy, implementation,
packaging or commissioning. Generate the next controlled revision
without destroying predecessor states.

stages.title: RETIRE
stages.prompt:
Retire the physical artefact while preserving provenance, configuration,
evidence, maintenance history, operational history and final status.
